drivingQuestion: From where do we know that all the impure are forbidden to eat teruma?
outcomeNote: The unit breaks off mid-derivation ('what matter is the same'); the answer continues in the next unit

segments.he: וְכׇל הַטְּמֵאִים כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אָמַר קְרָא: ״אִישׁ אִישׁ מִזֶּרַע אַהֲרֹן וְהוּא צָרוּעַ אוֹ זָב וְגוֹ׳״. אֵי זֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁשָּׁוֶה
segments.en: § It is taught in the mishna that «all» those «who are ritually impure» with any type of ritual impurity may not eat teruma. The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? «Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael: The verse states: “Any man from the seed of Aaron who is a leper or a zav» shall not eat of the holy things until he be pure” (Leviticus 22:4). Now, «what matter is the same»
